director_boundary.user_query: What can the association actually see?
director_boundary.ai_message:
Less than you might expect, and that is deliberate.

I can show you aggregates: how many schools submitted, how complete a section is, and a benchmark built from at least 5 contributing schools.

I cannot show you one school's own figures, a named school's detail, individual staff records, or any student-level data — test scores, assessment results, AP, IB, SAT, ACT or MAP among them. None of that is aggregated at the association, and no screen here drills into a single school.

I also cannot cut a result by country. AMISA has member countries with exactly one school in them, and a country cut identifies that school.

This is not a setting I am refusing to change. It is what the platform is allowed to answer.
suggested_chips: What is the average teacher salary for a master's degree with 3 years of experience?

director_participation.ai_message:
6 schools have not opened the Business Office section. Named, with a contact for each.

You do not have to build a spreadsheet. You send 6 emails.

One thing to be clear about: these 6 schools will not see the Business Office benchmark on October 1. Not as a punishment — it is the rule your RFP wrote. Office data is visible only to schools that entered it, and the platform enforces that. Nobody has to remember to.

director_completion.user_query: How many schools have finished the Human Resources section?
director_completion.ai_message:
29 of the 31 participating schools have submitted Human Resources. 88% of the questions in those submissions are complete.

By office, across everyone taking part this year:
Human Resources — 29 of 31 submitted.
Business Office — 25 of 31 submitted.

What you are not seeing here is any school's actual figures. This is submission status, not submitted data.

director_approvals.ai_message:
One request, from Cordillera International School.

Their head of school wants to ask the membership 4 questions. You can see who it would go to, when it opens and when it closes.

Approve it, send it back with a comment, or decline it. A question that used to be an email to 70 people becomes a survey with a window, reminders and a completion rate — and whether it goes out at all is your call.
suggested_chips: Send it back with a comment

director_approved.ai_message:
Approved and scheduled.

It opens Monday and closes in three weeks. Reminders go at day 7 and day 14. Cordillera will see the completion rate as it fills.

Approved by Dereck Rhoads. Audit trail recorded.

director_sent_back.user_query: Send it back with a comment
director_sent_back.ai_message:
Sent back to Cordillera with your note. Nothing goes to the membership.

They can revise and resubmit, and it will come back to this queue.

director_quality.ai_message:
312 responses swept. I found six things and fixed none of them.

Every row below is a proposal, not an action. Each one says why it was flagged, and each one is yours to keep or apply.

One of them I will not decide. Answering quickly is a judgement call, not a rule, so it comes to you unchecked.
suggested_chips: Why was the salary field flagged?

director_narrative_detail.user_query: Why was the salary field flagged?
director_narrative_detail.ai_message:
One school entered "varies by contract" where a number belongs.

That is the exact case you raised with us: text in a numeric field. It cannot be averaged, and guessing at what it meant would be worse than dropping it — so the record comes out of the salary benchmark and goes back to the school with a note.

The two figures far outside the range are a different problem. They read like a local-currency amount typed into a field defined as USD. I have not corrected them, because I do not know which currency was meant.

298 valid responses, from 312.

Applied by Dereck Rhoads. Audit trail recorded.

Every number after this point traces back to that decision. I did the sweep. You made the call.

Nothing excluded. All 312 records stay in the analysis set.

Applied by Dereck Rhoads. Audit trail recorded.

director_benchmark.user_query: What is the average teacher salary for a master's degree with 3 years of experience?
director_benchmark.ai_message:
$34,800.

From 24 schools. Base salary only, excluding housing and benefits, full-time equivalent.

The schools that did not submit are excluded from this answer — and from the access to it.
suggested_chips: Show a school with too few peers

director_peers.ai_message:
Here is Cordillera International School against schools like it.

It does not group by country. It groups by enrollment and tuition — which is how you described it to us.

18 schools in this peer group, against a floor of 5. Below that floor nothing renders at all.

The school in Chile is inside this number. Nobody looking at this screen can find it.
suggested_chips: Show a school with too few peers

director_suppressed.user_query: Show a school with too few peers
director_suppressed.ai_message:
This is what the floor actually does.

This school is one of the smallest in the membership, and only 2 contributing schools are close enough on enrollment and tuition to compare with. The minimum is 5.

So there is no number here. Not a rounded one, not an approximate one, not one with a warning next to it. The comparison does not render, and the school is told why.

That is the behaviour that makes a head of school willing to submit in the first place.

director_summary.ai_message:
Here is the association summary, ready for the schools that took part.

AMISA branded. Plain language. Every figure sourced.

When it reaches a school, that school sees its own number against a group it belongs to, and nothing else. The six schools that never opened the Business Office section receive the Human Resources sections only.

director_publish_confirm.ai_message:
This publishes to the 31 schools taking part this year. Each one receives only the sections it is entitled to.

Nothing goes to the 39 schools that are not participating.

director_published.ai_message:
Published.

31 schools notified. Each sees the sections it submitted, and its own figure against a peer group that meets the floor.

September 30 in. October 1 out. The cycle now runs without an inbox.
